suggestions.title: 1. The rest of the medical part: a whole version a round, or a line or two for each section?
suggestions.question:
Nine sections of the medical part read AI in the first batch and haven't been fixed: Call medics for, Who to Contact, Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue (these two paragraphs), My Brain Feels Damaged, Active Seizure's first part, MDMA's jaw tension, Chest Pain, Recent Oral Toxic Ingestion's charcoal and poison control paragraphs, and Serotonin Syndrome. How each option would go:

A: as now: one teaching card a round, and I carry what you do to the others and test them. Pro: you write one section a round. Con: my carries of your two medical versions read AI in all eight tries, so so far only the section you write turns Human.

B (my pick): next round, a short box for each of those sections, for a line or two of your own there: what you've seen, what you'd do, or what you think of the standard advice. I build each section around what you write and test it. Pro: the whole part in a round or two, and it's how my fixes went Human in the remedies, where something you wrote was near (Nausea Smoothers, DMSO, the ocean water). Con: untried on clinical text; a section that still reads AI comes back to you as a teaching card.
suggestions.why: Since round 34, every Human read in the medical part is a version you wrote, and none of my eight carries passed ([this round's four](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h45-20261112/RESULTS.md)). That changes how much a teaching round can do, so how to spend your time on the rest is your call.
suggestions.advice_note: B, not sure: it's where my fixes have read Human so far, but I haven't tried it on clinical text.

suggestions.sense: A fresh reader of my tries needed every pattern, the 38°C, "don't wait for all of them" and the call-for-help line, and found the name "the Hunter criteria" a source label the reader doesn't act on, so my tries leave it out. The guide's version names the five patterns by their clinical terms ("Spontaneous clonus", "Inducible clonus plus agitation or sweating", "Tremor plus hyperreflexia", ...), most of which a reader would have to look up in the moment.
suggestions.why: Its shape, the signs that point to one condition, is the medical part's third common shape after the two you taught (when to get help; what to find out, then decide): Chest Pain's warning signs, the checks in My Brain Feels Damaged and the Call medics list share it. It's also the largest part of the guide that reads AI (the whole section, 512 words).
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: say how you'd tell someone to recognize serotonin toxicity, in your words. Keep the five patterns, each with its companion sign, and the 38°C (100.4°F); the last line's "dangerous", "deserves" and "rigidity" are kept as warnings, so keep those words or say they can change. Whatever you pick on card 1, your version goes in whole, and I test what it teaches on the sections above.
